name: esedb_query
description: Read an ESE database (WebCacheV01.dat, SRUDB.dat, spartan.edb) as TABLES through esedbexport: list the tables, or return the rows of one, each row numbered by its position in the exported file. It exports tables as text and decodes nothing: a SRUM table is not joined to the application or user it names, a WebCache container is not resolved, and an ESE log is not read. The export is made once per database into esedb-export/<db sha256, first 16 hex>/ under the job's $OUT (or the agent's work directory), with the exporter's whole stdout and stderr in files beside it and an export-manifest.json (database digest, exporter version, argv, exit status, every table file); a complete export is reused by later calls only when its manifest was written by this version, its exit status was 0, and every table file it lists is on disk with its recorded size and nothing else is there (otherwise it is exported again). An exporter that exits non-zero or is stopped by export_timeout_seconds leaves a PARTIAL export: status partial, complete false, the tables listed only as tables_in_partial_export, never as the database's tables. A table name that matches more than one export file is refused with the candidates. The table file is read as the exporter wrote it, as tab-separated text with a row to a line and no quoting rule (a quote or a carriage return is a character of its cell), and _row is the 1-based line of the row after the header. A column name that repeats, or is named like a key the answer adds (_row), is numbered. What an answer prints inline is bounded: the rows that fit limit and 256 KiB, with a cell longer than 4,096 characters shown cut (_cells_shortened names it); every row with every cell whole is in the JSON Lines file all_results names, written whenever the inline rows are not the whole of the table, and never replaced by another result. A row longer than 8 MiB is read to that length and said to be cut (it is whole in the export). The tool stops at its own time limit (285 seconds) with the rows read and says partial. Every answer carries status (complete, partial, failed) and status_basis. SENSITIVE: the export directory holds every table whole, so whatever the database holds (a WebCache URL with a token, SRUM users, the password material of an Active Directory database, which NTDS.dit is): it is made mode 0700 with files 0600, is a sensitive output of the job that made it, and is cited by file and table, never by value; run it as a job with secret_output: true when the case may. The rows returned withhold, with a marker holding only the length, the cells of a column whose name says password, secret, token, encrypted, credential, a card, an IBAN or an SSN, and of the datatable attributes that carry password hashes, their history, supplemental credentials and the password encryption keys (columns_withheld lists them); the credential-named query and fragment parameters of a URL in a cell, and a password in its user-info, are withheld the same way, by parameter name and shape (url_secrets_withheld lists them; a secret in a URL's path or in a title, a user-info token of another shape such as one holding a slash, and free text are NOT covered and are printed; write_url_secrets: true writes the whole text of the URLs withheld to a 0600 file under $OUT, in a job only). Binary cells are exported as hex text and are not inspected, so a WebCache header column can still hold a cookie: cite, do not copy. The program runs in the tool's own process group (never a session of its own), so the harness ending the tool ends it; the tool's own deadline kills it and what it started, and SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP do the same and the answer is then status interrupted.

table.description: Table to read; omit to list the tables

limit.description: Rows shown inline at most (default 200, at most 20000, an inline page size; the inline rows are also held to 256 KiB, so fewer may be shown); every row is kept whole, and when the inline rows are not the whole table the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

export_timeout_seconds.description: How long to let esedbexport run (default 240, at most 270); a run that is stopped keeps what it wrote and the answer says partial

write_url_secrets.description: Write the whole text of every URL whose secrets were withheld, with the secret value, to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
